If something is pneumatic, it contains or operates by air or gas under pressure.
The branch of mechanics that deals with the mechanical properties of gases
A gram-positive bacterium, Streptococcus pneumoniae, that causes pneumonia and other infectious diseases.
A parasitic fungal organism of the genus Pneumocystis, in humans specifically Pneumocystis jorevicii.
Pneumonia is an acute or chronic inflammation of the lungs caused by viruses, bacteria or other microorganisms.
A medicine to treat lung disease.
If something is pneumonic, it is related to the lungs or pneumonia.
Inflammation of the tissue of the lungs.
Presence of air inside the pleural cavity, usually caused by injury either to the lung or the chest wall.
